kings1.9.p1.b1.text: Now when Solomon had finished building the house of the LORD and the royal palace, and had achieved all that he had desired to do,

kings1.9.p1.b2.text: the LORD appeared to him a second time, as He had appeared to him at Gibeon.

kings1.9.p1.b3.text: I have heard your prayer and petition before Me. I have consecrated this temple you have built by putting My Name there forever; My eyes and My heart will be there for all time.

kings1.9.p1.b4.text: And as for you, if you walk before Me as your father David walked, with a heart of integrity and uprightness …

kings1.9.p1.b5.text: then I will establish your royal throne over Israel forever …

kings1.9.p2.b1.text: But if indeed you or your sons turn away from following Me … and if you go off to serve and worship other gods

kings1.9.p2.b2.text: … and I will banish from My presence this temple I have sanctified for My Name …

kings1.9.p2.b3.text: And when this temple has become a heap of rubble, all who pass by it will be appalled and will hiss and say, ‘Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land and to this temple?’

kings1.9.p2.b4.text: And others will answer, ‘Because they have forsaken the LORD their God who brought their fathers out of the land of Egypt, and have embraced other gods …

kings1.9.p3.b1.text: Now at the end of the twenty years during which Solomon built these two houses, the house of the LORD and the royal palace,

kings1.9.p3.b2.text: So Hiram went out from Tyre to inspect the towns that Solomon had given him, but he was not pleased with them.

kings1.9.p3.b3.text: What are these towns you have given me, my brother?

kings1.9.p3.b4.text: … and he called them the Land of Cabul, as they are called to this day.

kings1.9.p4.b1.text: This is the account of the forced labor that King Solomon imposed to build the house of the LORD, his own palace, the supporting terraces, and the wall of Jerusalem, as well as Hazor, Megiddo …

kings1.9.p4.b2.text: So Solomon rebuilt Gezer, Lower Beth-horon, Baalath, and Tamar in the Wilderness of Judah,

kings1.9.p4.b3.text: their descendants who remained in the land, those whom the Israelites were unable to devote to destruction —Solomon conscripted these people to be forced laborers, as they are to this day.

kings1.9.p4.b4.text: But Solomon did not consign any of the Israelites to slavery, because they were his men of war, his servants, his officers, his captains, and the commanders of his chariots and cavalry.

kings1.9.p5.b1.text: Three times a year Solomon offered burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar he had built for the LORD … So he completed the temple.

kings1.9.p5.b2.text: King Solomon also assembled a fleet of ships at Ezion-geber, which is near Eloth in Edom, on the shore of the Red Sea.

kings1.9.p5.b3.text: And Hiram sent his servants, men who knew the sea, to serve in the fleet with Solomon’s servants.

kings1.9.p5.b4.text: They sailed to Ophir and imported gold from there—420 talents —and delivered it to Solomon.
